newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGBs end Tokyo lower, eyes on 'tankan' survey.
newsitem.headline: Key JGBs end Tokyo lower, eyes on 'tankan' survey.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended lower on Tuesday, as market sentiment weakened after a fall in U.S. Treasury bond prices overnight.
"The December's decline was due to a fall in U.S. Treasuries," said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
"The fall was also due to position adjustment ahead of the 'tankan' corporate sentiment survey and the announcement of the six-year JGB auction results," the trader added.
The December closed at 119.25, down from Monday's 119.50, after moving within a range of 119.21 to 119.40 during the day.
Roll-over sales from the September to the new benchmark December futures contract may also have contributed to the fall of the December, traders said.
"Few traders are selling the September while there is substantial selling pressure on the December contract," the trader said.
The selling of the December may be for hedging purposes, and not just roll-overs from the previous benchmark, the trader added.
The Finance Ministry offered about 500 billion yen worth of six-year JGBs through an auction on Tuesday.
The lowest price of the 2.3 percent six-year JGBs sold through the auction was 99.19, while the average price was 99.25.

A trader for a trust bank's securities unit said there were rumours that some investors had sold, in the morning, 10-year JGBs with six-year maturities in order to replace them with the newly auctioned six-year JGBs.
Most traders said, however, investors showed little inclination to move ahead of the Bank of Japan's "tankan" corporate sentiment survey to be released on Wednesday.
The BOJ is unlikely to raise interest rates based solely on the results of the key corporate survey, traders said.

"I don't expect the 'tankan' results to deviate much from the previous survey's forecast figures. The market consensus is that the tankan results will show the economy to be recovering very gradually," the first trader said.
"Unless the diffusion index for big manufacturers comes in at plus three or over or minus five and below, there will be little impact on the market," a trust bank trader said.
The key 182nd cash JGB was yielding 3.145 percent as of 0708 GMT, up from Monday's 3.115 percent.
